subject: Clarify billing quantum, long-context banding, and pilot concession
messages:

Subject: Billing mechanics question — token quantum & long-context behavior

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. As we build the cost model for our product team, we need a precise description of how Redwood will meter a few edge scenarios so we can map to our P&L and to the invoice format our finance team expects. Attached is a small sample of our call mix for June (ACME_usage_sample.csv). Key questions below — can you confirm in writing?

1) Quantum/rounding: If you charge in 100-token increments, does every call round up to the nearest increment independently? If so, do streaming responses get rounded per API call or per response chunk?

2) Long context: We expect many calls to include 32k+ context (history + embeddings). Do you have slab pricing or surcharges for >16k contexts, or is that just expressed in heavier per-token unit cost?

3) Minimums & microbursts: Our team can have long quiet periods followed by short spikes of many tiny calls (10–50 tokens). Is there an available microburst pool or smoothing concession to avoid massive rounding waste? What does an exception pilot look like?

4) Prefix reuse and KV cache: We reuse the same prefix in ~40% of calls — any automatic prefix crediting that reduces billable tokens? If so, how is that shown on the invoice?

We want a short example table we can forward to finance (3 example calls with before/after math). Also please indicate any contract language (MAA) we should expect around billing rounding and pilot concessions.

Best,
Lena
Director, ML Product
Acme Retail

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Billing mechanics question — token quantum & long-context behavior

Hi Lena — thanks for the sample, that helps. High level answers first, then a short worked example. Attaching our proposed pricing sheet and a short example calc.

Short answers:
- Quantum/rounding: Yes — hosted API charges are rounded to a 100-token quantum by default (we call it the metering quantum). Rounding happens per API request (per call). For streaming, we round per completed request (so a single streaming response is billed once at the final token count, rounded to quantum).
- Long context: We have discrete context tiers (4k, 16k, 64k). For >16k we recommend the 64k variant which uses a blended per-token rate (lower than on-demand 16k overage). There is an optional long-context surcharge model for custom workloads.
- Microbursts: We offer pilot smoothing: an allocation pool (microburst credits) that auto-applies to small calls under a threshold to reduce rounding overhead. For pilots we can (a) provide a temporary credit pool for the first 2 months, and (b) reduce the effective quantum to 25 tokens for a defined set of API keys during the pilot window.
- Prefix reuse/KV cache: We automatically apply prefix caching credits where the same prefix is reused within a session boundary. That shows on the invoice as a % KV credit line and a reduced effective token count for those calls.

Worked example (attached as spreadsheet; summarized here):
1) Short call: prompt=45 tokens, response=55 tokens => total 100 tokens => billed 100 (1 quantum)
2) Tiny calls burst: prompt=12 tokens, response=18 tokens => total 30 tokens => rounded to 100 (3.33x alpha). With pilot microburst pool (25-token quantum) billed = 50 -> effective saving 50 tokens per call.
3) Long context call: prompt+history=14k, response=1.2k => total 15.2k tokens => billed at 15.2k rounded => 15.2k rounds to 15.2k (since quantum applies in 100 increments, effectively 15,200 -> 15,200). If using 64k model, per-token rate is 12% lower; if long-context surcharge model applies, we would list as separate invoice line.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal review (Ben & Camila) to confirm concession math and guardrails.
- If okay, we'll add a 2-month microburst credit clause to a pilot Appendix A to the MAA (redlines to be shared).
- We'll prepare a short three-line invoice example you can send to Acme finance.

Attaching: RI_proposed_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf, rounding_calculations.xlsx

Best,
Avery
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Avery / team / Lena — quick confirmation and operational notes. Agree to the pilot; here's how to frame and the safe-guards.

Operational approach:
- Credit pool: 500k microburst credits dedicated to ACME (non-transferrable). Credits apply only to calls with total tokens <100. Credits are consumed first; after depletion normal billing resumes.
- Quantum override: for pilot API keys we set metering quantum = 25 tokens for the pilot window. This is implemented as a flag; usage is still audited and visible in the token-level export.
- Abuse controls: rate limits (QPS) per-key and an anomaly detector that flags >10x average burst size per 5m window. If flagged, we auto-suspend quantum override for that key and notify both teams.

Example math snippets (see attached rounding_calculations.xlsx):
- Micro call: 30 tokens => normally rounds to 100 => billed 100 at $0.0002/token => $0.02. With microburst credit pool charged 0 => invoice shows a negative credit line consuming credits.
- Long call 15,200 tokens => billed at 15,200 tokens (rounded to 100 token quantum) => invoice shows 15,200 @ long-context per-token rate. If ACME is on 64k slab, rate per token is reduced by 12% (line item shows slab applied).

Contract language to include in Appendix A (summary):
- Pilot duration: 60 days from start date.
- Credits: 500,000 microburst credits applied to calls <100 tokens.
- Quantum override: temporary metering quantum = 25 tokens while pilot active.
- Monitoring & rollback: Redwood reserves the right to disable override on suspicious activity; Redwood will provide artifacted logs for any disablement event.

I'll let Legal draft precise MAA appendix wording but this is the safe, well-used pattern.

Ben
